hooks.text: Does a full moon really trigger human madness?
The twenty-eight day human cycle is a mathematical mismatch for the moon.
Centuries of data show the lunar effect is a complete scientific myth.

title: The Truth About the Lunar Effect
description: Decades of data prove the full moon has no influence on crime, births, or human behavior.

beats.text: Does a full moon really trigger human madness?
beats.visual: photograph of the full moon seen through a telescope, 2024

beats.text: For centuries, medical staff and police have blamed the lunar cycle for spikes in chaos.
beats.visual: photograph of a hospital emergency room entrance at night, 2021

beats.text: However, meta-analyses of over one hundred studies show zero correlation with human behavior.
beats.visual: digital illustration of statistical data graphs and lunar phases, 2022

beats.text: Even the twenty-eight day human cycle is a mismatch for the twenty-nine point five day lunar month.
beats.visual: infographic comparing the lunar month and human biological cycles, 2023

beats.text: Research finds no link between moon phases and birth rates, homicide, or the number of suicides.
beats.visual: photograph of blue police cruiser lights at a distance at night, 2022

beats.text: While the moon pulls entire oceans, its gravity is far too weak to impact human physiology.
beats.visual: photograph of high tide ocean waves crashing against sea cliffs, 2021

beats.text: Higher tides at the full moon occur because the Sun, Earth, and Moon align in space.
beats.visual: diagram showing the gravitational alignment of the Sun, Earth, and Moon, 2022

beats.text: Coral species sync their lives to moonlight, but human actions remain grounded in science.
beats.visual: photograph of coral polyps spawning in the ocean at night, 2020

beats.text: Yet despite zero scientific proof, the ancient myth survives.
beats.visual: photograph of the full moon shining brightly in a dark night sky, 2024

better_than_last: This script implements a question-based hook and addresses the 28-day cycle mismatch as a central twist to improve retention.
